GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual by seeking to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensuring women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

Article 67
Funding for the implementation of the Gender and Child data system is sourced from the state revenue and expenditure budget, the provincial regional revenue and expenditure budget and the Regional revenue and expenditure budget as well as other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Part Two Fulfillment of Women's Rights
Article 13
The fulfillment of women's rights is the obligation and responsibility of:
a. every person, b. family, c. community organizations,
d. business actors,
e. f.
Village Government: and Regional Government.
Paragraph Obligations and Responsibilities of Every Person in the Fulfillment of Women's Rights Article 14 Every person in the fulfillment of women's rights has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. not smoke in work spaces where there are female workers who are pregnant or breastfeeding, b. maintain the honor and dignity of women in accordance with religious norms and customs, c. prevent the occurrence of discriminatory, exploitative, and intimidating actions against women, d. report to the authorities if aware of any acts of violation of women's rights, and
e. prevent the occurrence of violations of women's rights.
Paragraph Obligations and Responsibilities of Family Members in the Fulfillment of Women's Rights

Article 37
The Village Government in fulfilling the rights and Protection of Children has the obligations and responsibilities: (1)
a. formulating policies in the field of Child Protection, b. facilitating the establishment of Child organizations at the village level,
c. providing budget to support activities for the fulfillment of rights and Protection of child victims of violence and Children who require Special Protection at the Village level, d. compiling child profile data at the Village level,
e. implementing the implementation of Child-friendly Village in programs and activities of the village revenue and expenditure budget,
f. providing education scholarship budget for underprivileged Children,
g. providing budget for Integrated Service Posts (Posyandu) at the Village level, h. providing budget for Early Childhood Education management institutions, i. preventing the occurrence of violence and exploitation of Children,
j. preventing attempts to take Children out of the Village/Region without parental permission and the knowledge of the Village Head, and k. making efforts to fulfill the rights of Children who require Special Protection.
(2) In the event that the Village Government does not fulfill the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, letter f, letter g, and letter h, the Regional Government may postpone the distribution or reduce the allocation of village funds.
(3) The procedures and percentage amounts of budgeting as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, letter f, letter g, and letter h as well as the postponement of distribution or reduction of village fund allocation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 76
The Regional Puspa Forum conducts evaluation and reporting (1) annually.
The annual evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted (one) time in (one) year or at any time if necessary.
(2) The annual reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented (one) time in (one) year or (3) at any time if necessary.
In addition to the annual reporting as referred to in (4) paragraph (3), the Regional level Puspa Forum conducts periodic reporting before the end of the forum membership period.
The reporting of the Regional level Puspa Forum is submitted (5) to the Regent with a copy to the Governor.

CHAPTER VII
INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING AND DEVELOPMENT Article 61 (1) Regional Governments are responsible for strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection existing in the Region.
(2) In strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as referred to in paragraph (1), Regional Governments shall provide budget in accordance with the Region's financial capacity.

CHAPTER XV
CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 88
The Implementing Regulations of this Regional Regulation must be established no later than (one) year calculated from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

Article 19
(1) The Village Government in fulfilling women's rights has the obligations and responsibilities to:
a. formulate policies in the field of women's empowerment at the Village level,
b. facilitate the establishment of women's organizations at the Village level,
c. provide budget to support empowerment activities for dasawisma groups and women's groups at the Village level,
d. compile profile data of women at the Village level,
e. implement the implementation of women-friendly and Child-caring Villages in the programs and activities of the village revenue and expenditure budget,
f. increase women's representation in the structure of Village apparatus, membership of the Village Consultative Body, and management of Village customary institutions,
g. increase women entrepreneurs in the Village,
h. increase women's involvement in the management of village revenue and expenditure budget, and
i. make efforts to fulfill women's rights.
(2) In the event that the village government does not fulfill the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, the Regional Government may postpone the distribution or reduce the allocation of village funds.
(3) The procedures and percentage amount of budgeting as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c as well as the postponement of distribution or reduction of village fund allocation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 75
(1) The Regional level Puspa Forum in carrying out the task of coordinating as referred to in Article 74 paragraph (1) is conducted in the form of:
a. Regional level coordination,
b. sectoral coordination, and
c. special coordination.
(2) Regional level coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented at least once (one time) in one (one) year or at any time when necessary to strengthen communication, cooperation, and discuss the implementation of the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection at the Regional level.
(3) Sectoral coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented periodically at least once (one time) in four (four) months or at any time when necessary to discuss program activities that are its duties.
(4) Special coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in the event it is necessary to resolve special problems that require quick and precise solutions related to the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 39
Regional Government in the effort to fulfill the rights and Protection of Children has the obligations and responsibilities:
a. to formulate short, medium, and long-term strategic plans for Child protection, b. to provide legal aid facilities in the form of advocacy and assistance for victims and or families of victims of violence against Children, c. to encourage the responsibility of all stakeholders to fulfill obligations and responsibilities in fulfilling the rights and Protection of Children, d. to provide budget for programs for the fulfillment of rights and Protection of Children at the Regional level,
e. to facilitate the establishment of children's organizations at the Regional level,
f. to provide shelter facilities for child victims of violence, and
g. to coordinate the implementation of the fulfillment of rights and Protection of Children in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 70 is carried out in:
a. providing input at the stage of formation of laws and regulations,
b. planning and budgeting, c. implementation, and
d. monitoring and evaluation, regarding Women's Empowerment and Child Protection carried out by Regional Government and Village Government.
Community participation in providing input at (2) the stage of formation of laws and regulations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter is carried out by providing input regarding the substance of Gender Equality, protection of women's rights, Fulfillment of Children's rights, and Special Protection of Children so that:
a. in accordance with the needs of women and Children, b. non-discriminatory towards women and Children, c. providing convenience and special treatment towards women and Children.
Community participation in planning and (3) budgeting as referred to in paragraph (1) letter is carried out by integrating Gender perspective and Children's rights into community programs and activities.
Community participation in implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) letter is carried out by conducting partnerships with Regional Government which are carried out in the form of: (4)
a. strengthening the institutionalization of Women's Empowerment and institutionalization of Child Protection, b. strengthening or increasing the capacity of women in access, participation, control, and benefits in all fields of development through technical guidance and supervision,
c. mutually providing facilitation support or assistance (specific needs of women and special needs of Children) in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations,
d. providing information through socialization and advocacy regarding women's rights and Children's rights as well as laws and regulations concerning women and Children,
e. preventing the occurrence of violence and human rights violations against women and Children including in conflict and disaster situations,
f. reporting if violence occurs against women and Children,
g. assisting women victims of violence so that they do not experience stigma and exclusion in their environment, h. supporting the availability of facilities and infrastructure in creating a conducive atmosphere for the growth and participation of Children,
i. playing an active role in eliminating negative labeling towards Children, and
j. supporting the development of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection developed in Regions and Villages including women-friendly and child-caring Villages.

7.5.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly states provincial budget as a funding source for the Gender and Child data system: Pasal 67 includes “anggaran pendapatan dan belanja daerah provinsi”. That is the provincial government budget (APBD Provinsi). Therefore the predicted “Yes” is correct and the golden label “No” appears wrong.
